note: Both sets capture the same core engineering facts correctly: window azimuth 0 for the southern louver, 50-degree solar altitude at fall equinox 12pm, the depth-to-height algorithm, the 25-degree structural bend, and the 1:1 louver depth-to-height ratio. Set A adds a second, redundant 'louver | shape | truncated isosceles triangle' claim that duplicates its own conditioned claim, so it repeats the same fact under the same names. Both sets also repeat the 50-degree solar altitude under two entity/attribute framings ('Harvest Shade Screen | solar altitude' and the vague 'solar altitude | value'). Because Set B carries the same correct content with one fewer duplicate, it is marginally better.
remarks: Both sets truncate quotes mid-word ('windo', 'longit'), which weakens evidentiary support though the underlying readings are correct. Both also omit the fact that louver spacing was proportionally reduced based on the average of the profile widths after the taper, and the simplified relation Height = D*1.2; these are notable omissions shared by both sets. The 'solar altitude | value' claim is a vague restatement of the better-formed Harvest Shade Screen solar altitude claim in both sets.
